question:

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Goal: Determine average additional cost per over-limit file given an upgrade to the minimum plan that fits all files. FileSurfer, please open and read the attached image for plan names, storage capacities, and monthly prices.

history.content:
Opened image: d8152ad6-e4d5-4c12-8bb7-8d57dc10c6de.png. Extracted details from the pricing table visible:

- Plus: 2 TB included storage, $25/month
- Business: 10 TB included storage, $60/month
- Enterprise: 20 TB included storage, $110/month
Notes on the image: “No overage add-ons available; upgrade required to increase storage.” The Standard plan clearly shows 500 GB limit and $12/mo price.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Thanks. Assistant, please compute the per-file size using the overage hint: After uploading 60 files, the user is 100 GB over the 500 GB Standard limit. So 60 × size = 500 GB + 100 GB. Solve for file size.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Let s be per-file size in GB. 60s = 500 + 100 = 600 GB, so s = 10 GB per file.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Next, compute total storage needed for all 1040 files and identify the minimal plan tier that accommodates that total, based on FileSurfer’s extracted tiers.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Total storage = 1040 files × 10 GB/file = 10,400 GB = 10.4 TB. The tiers listed are 2 TB (Plus), 10 TB (Business), and 20 TB (Enterprise). Business at 10 TB is slightly under 10.4 TB, so it won’t fit. The minimum plan that fits 10.4 TB is Enterprise at 20 TB.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Confirm how many files are covered by the Standard plan storage and how many are over the Standard limit when considering all 1040 files.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Standard storage is 500 GB. At 10 GB per file, Standard covers 500/10 = 50 files. The number of files over the current plan limit is 1040 − 50 = 990 files.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Compute the additional monthly cost of upgrading from Standard to Enterprise using the extracted prices.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Enterprise is $110/month; Standard is $12/month. Additional monthly cost = $110 − $12 = $98/month.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Now compute the average additional cost per file that is over the Standard limit: divide the additional monthly cost by 990 and round to the nearest cent.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Average additional cost per over-limit file = $98 ÷ 990 ≈ $0.098989... Rounded to the nearest cent: $0.10.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Total needed is 10,400 GB; Standard provides 500 GB. Shortfall is 10,400 − 500 = 9,900 GB. At 10 GB per file, that corresponds to 9,900/10 = 990 files over the limit. This matches the previous count.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Confirm that Enterprise (20 TB) is indeed the minimum plan that can handle 10.4 TB, given the tier list, and that no intermediate tier exists between 10 TB and 20 TB in the image.
